why: This asks you to build the heap itself: store values in an array as a complete binary tree, sift up on push and sift down on pop, so the minimum is always at index 0.
hints: A sorted list gives O(n) inserts; with 2*10^5 operations you want O(log n).
Use an array where the children of i are 2i+1 and 2i+2 and every parent is <= its children; the minimum is at index 0.
PUSH: append and swap upward while smaller than the parent. POP: save a[0], move the last element to index 0, then swap downward with the smaller child. PEEK reads a[0]. O(log n) per op.
pitfalls: When sifting down, compare with the smaller of the two children, and check that the right child exists.
Popping the last remaining element: remove it without sifting an empty array.
Duplicates are allowed; use < (not <=) in comparisons to avoid needless swaps, either works for correctness.
values[i] is ignored for PEEK and POP.
